title: Real agents, OSO vs traditional: race-cheap

design.question: With the cheapest model, does an OSO community of AI labs solve more of the hard targets than a traditional one, for the same money?
design.fixed: four DeepSeek V4.1 Flash labs (two foundation builders, a target racer, a neutral lab), $0.15 each, 12 posted conjectures, up to 30 rounds
design.measure: counted targets solved (A3, X2, B5, A5)

answer: No clear difference: the OSO communities solved 2.0 of the counted targets and the traditional ones 1.6, on average over 5 runs each.
caveats: Counted targets: those DeepSeek never proved alone in the pilot but did with lemmas; neither side reached B5 or A5.
One model and one small problem set; 4 traditional actions were lost to dropped connections, none on the OSO side.
Budgets were not binding: the communities spent 52% of theirs on average, because labs passed.
Values are mean ± standard deviation over runs.
